assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology (incretin action, proglucagon processing, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, appetite and gastric effects) led to therapies that have transformed type 2 diabetes and obesity care. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are all very high, and the path from basic physiology to a widely used medicine is unusually complete.
assessment.attribution: Holst (physiology and secretion of GLP-1 in humans), Drucker (GLP-1 and GLP-2 biology, proglucagon-derived peptides) and Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) form and its insulinotropic action) form a coherent three-person configuration. Knudsen (liraglutide/semaglutide development) is a credible alternative, and the Habener contribution is not in the supplied credit list; the allocation is contested and I cannot resolve it from the longlist text alone.
assessment.maturity: Clinical efficacy and cardiometabolic outcomes are confirmed by large independent trials and mass adoption; the basic mechanism is stable. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Credit among Mojsov, Habener, Holst, Drucker and Knudsen is disputed; the exact fair three-person set is uncertain.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history, not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new mode of organelle-to-nucleus signaling and proteostasis control, with consequences for secretory biology, diabetes, neurodegeneration and cancer. A clean, conceptually original discovery with a clear mechanistic chain (IRE1, HAC1/XBP1 splicing).
assessment.attribution: Walter (IRE1 as the sensor, the UPR pathway in yeast and mammals) and Mori (the UPR transcriptional response and HAC1/XBP1 and ATF6 axis) are the natural pair. Attribution is relatively clean; Ron (ISR/PERK) and others could be argued as additional contributors but are not in the supplied credits.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent confirmation, widely taught in cell biology, and a Lasker award history. The basic discovery is mature; therapeutic translation is still partial.
uncertainties: Therapeutic impact is still emerging, so the claim rests mainly on conceptual significance.
Whether the prize should extend to the integrated stress response is outside the supplied credits.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and has been transformative for circuit analysis, including motor and spinal circuits. The tool is original, general and enormously used, and early clinical applications (vision restoration) are appearing.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin identification and characterization, with Bamberg) and Deisseroth (neuronal implementation, tools and broad application) are the strongest three-person set. Boyden and Miesenböck made early or parallel neuronal demonstrations, and Bamberg's role is also strong; with six credited names any three leaves out a decisive contributor.
assessment.maturity: Very widely validated across labs and species; impact is established. Recognition is timely or somewhat overdue, but this is a technology prize with the usual question of tool versus discovery.
uncertainties: Six credited people with contested priority of the first neuronal demonstration.
Tool-development category rather than a discovery about disease.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR as the central regulator of cell growth, nutrient sensing and metabolism is a foundational concept with relevance to cancer, immunology, aging and metabolic disease, plus the clinical use of rapamycin analogs.
assessment.attribution: Hall discovered TOR genetically in yeast and established it as a growth regulator; Schreiber's chemical-biology work defined FKBP12-rapamycin action and the target. Sabatini's mammalian mTORC1 and mTORC2 work is important, but I would be cautious about including him given the supplied list alone; the allocation is open and a Hall-centered prize is also plausible.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed over decades with extensive independent literature and established clinical use of rapalogs. Mature.
uncertainties: Credit allocation between yeast genetics, chemical biology and mammalian mTOR biology is unresolved.
Clinical benefit of rapalogs is narrower than the biological importance of the pathway.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered CAR-T cells created a new class of living therapy producing durable remissions in refractory B-cell leukemias and lymphomas, and are expanding to myeloma and autoimmune settings. Strong clinical and conceptual impact.
assessment.attribution: June (CD19/4-1BB clinical translation) and Sadelain (CD28 costimulated CARs and preclinical foundations) are a good pair. Rosenberg's adoptive-cell-therapy work is also decisive for the clinic; Eshhar's original chimeric-receptor concept is not in the supplied credits, which complicates a fair configuration.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and independent confirmation across centers; long-term follow-up and toxicity profiles are still being defined. Mostly mature.
uncertainties: The originating chimeric-receptor concept is attributed outside the supplied credit list.
Limited efficacy in solid tumors and long-term safety remain open.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-term potentiation is the best-established cellular model of activity-dependent synaptic plasticity and underpins the synaptic basis of learning and memory. Originality and lasting influence are very high.
assessment.attribution: Lømo and Bliss made the original discovery in the rabbit hippocampus; Collingridge established NMDA-receptor dependence and mechanism. Morris's behavioral link (spatial learning, NMDA blockade) is also important, so a fair set requires omitting one of four.
assessment.maturity: Over fifty years of replication, but the causal link between LTP and memory storage is still debated, and there is limited direct disease or therapeutic translation. Timing is not premature, if anything overdue.
uncertainties: Which of Morris and Collingridge to include.
Mechanistic debate about LTP as the memory engram.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Splice-switching antisense therapy for spinal muscular atrophy (nusinersen) turned a lethal pediatric neuromuscular disease into a treatable one and validated antisense oligonucleotide medicine at the splicing level.
assessment.attribution: Krainer (mechanistic splicing regulation of SMN2 and ASO design principles) and Bennett (oligonucleotide chemistry and development at Ionis) are a clear pair. Other contributors (Hua, Singh, Adrian-Krainer collaborators, Biogen) are not in the credit list, and the SMN1 gene discovery by Melki and Lefebvre is separate.
assessment.maturity: Approved since 2016 with strong clinical outcomes and long-term follow-up; approach extended to other targets. Mature in clinical terms.
uncertainties: Platform-level credit for antisense chemistry might be split from the SMA-specific discovery.
Long-term durability across the SMA spectrum is still being documented.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: cGAS-STING identified how cytosolic DNA triggers innate immunity, with implications for infection, autoimmunity, interferonopathies and cancer immunotherapy. A clear mechanistic discovery with broad conceptual reach.
assessment.attribution: Chen (cGAS and the cyclic dinucleotide second messenger cGAMP) and Barber (STING) are the central contributors. Credits for Sun, Wu and Ishikawa reflect important contributions to the same pathway; Vance, Patel and others are not in the list, so allocation is incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Strongly reproduced, but therapeutic translation (STING agonists and inhibitors) has not yet delivered clear clinical success, so the discovery may be somewhat early for recognition.
uncertainties: Clinical validation is limited so far.
Credit among STING discoverers and cGAS/cGAMP contributors is uncertain.
